speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: asked the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources what is the number of water pipe leaks each year for the past 10 years.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: PUB has a stringent pipe laying regime to ensure that pipelines are well designed and implemented.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: PUB also constantly looks out for improved methods and materials, for example, the use of more corrosion-resistant polyurethane coating.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: However, despite the best design and implementation, leaks do occur mainly because of corrosion, uneven soil settlement or damage from construction work.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: Corrosion and soil settlement can impact all pipes, especially as they age.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: PUB has a comprehensive leak detection process to pick up leaks as early as possible.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: PUB conducts physical checks of its entire pipe network at least once a year, or more frequently where necessary.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: Portable acoustic leak noise data loggers are used to aid leak detection.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: Beyond detecting leaks, PUB has a Pipe Renewal Programme to pro-actively replace older pipes or pipes which are more prone to leaks due to local conditions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: For leaks due to construction damage, PUB takes tough action against errant parties, which could include the issue of a stop work notice to cease construction activities immediately and the imposition of financial penalties if pipes are damaged.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: When leaks occur, PUB seeks to fix them quickly.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: Most instances are resolved within a few hours.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: Occasionally, due to the need to ensure that water supply to residents is not disrupted when leaking pipelines are isolated from the rest of the network, more time is required to switch residents over to an alternative supply pipeline before the affected pipeline can be shut off.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: Water is precious and everybody needs to do his or her part to conserve it.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: Does the Member still have supplementary questions after such a long reply?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: I believe the Senior Minister of State said, on average, it is six leaks per 100 km over the last seven years.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: But what I am trying to get at is has the number been increasing, decreasing or remaining more or less the same?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: The second one is: will the PUB consider publishing this data on an annual basis if that is not being done right now?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: I say that also in the context of the statement that we have one of the best rates of water leakage in the world, which is commendable.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: I presume that that is using data that is published from other countries.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: So, presumably, other countries do publish this data.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: So, if that is not being done, will that data on the number of leaks per year be published on a regular basis?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: My third and last supplementary question: is the PUB working or moving beyond just leak detection and response towards proactive leak anticipation or prediction?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: I believe that there are research projects and there are initiatives in other parts of the world – I am not sure if that is being done in Singapore – where models are constructed using data to predict and anticipate where a fault or a leak is likely to occur, so that preventive action can be taken before the leak actually occurs.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: I know in Sydney, this has been going on for some time.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: The Water Research Foundation believes that through failure prediction —

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: Mr Leon, can you round up your question?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: So, through the creation of software models that take into account different factors we can anticipate that.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: So, is that being done or can that be considered to be done?

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: With regard to the first set of questions about the trend in the incidence rate of the leaks, I would say that, generally, it has been hovering around there for the last seven years.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, that has been the general trend in the numbers.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: There has been no discernible uptrend in the leak incidence rates.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: With regard to publication, we will take the Member's suggestions on board.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: But from time to time, we do actually report and publish such rates in any case.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: For the other countries, we also get information from published literature but I am not sure if everyone publishes it on an annual basis or on a regular basis.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As I have said, we have one of the lowest incidence in the world.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In Sydney, Australia, it is 28 leaks per 100 km.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: These are some of the data that we have.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: With regard to proactively identifying leaks, as I have said, we have a comprehensive leak management programme.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In fact, in more hotspot areas where leaks may occur because of soil condition and all that, we inspect it even more than once – maybe up to two to three times a year.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In addition, proactively, we also have a pipe renewal system.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The average age of our pipe network is about 25 years, which is actually well within the useful lifespan of these pipelines.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We have been able to do this because since the 1980s, we have an ongoing pipe renewal programme and we have been increasing the length of pipe that we replace each year.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We also do that with better materials, more corrosion-resistant materials.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We are constantly looking at improved methods and technologies to prevent or reduce leak incidence rates.
